explain.say: Every sound comes from something vibrating. Vibrating means moving back and forth very fast. Look at the wave on the board. Fast vibrations make a high pitch. Slow vibrations make a low pitch. Hum and touch your throat. You can feel it vibrate.

draw.name: x-wave
draw.note: More wobbles each second means a higher pitch

explain.say: Now look at the double bass. It is the biggest. It is about as tall as a grown-up. Its long, heavy strings vibrate slowly. So it plays the lowest notes. The small violin has short strings. It plays the highest notes.

explain.say: Look at the graph. When a string gets longer, its pitch goes down. When a string gets shorter, its pitch goes up. A guitar player presses a string to make it shorter. Then the note goes up.

Look at the violin again. It has the shortest strings and the highest pitch. Try this with a grown-up. Stretch a rubber band over a box and pluck it. Then stretch it tighter and pluck it again. Listen to how the pitch changes.

faq.a: Pitch is how high or low a sound is. A bird's tweet has a high pitch and a big drum has a low pitch.
asks: What makes a note high or low?

faq.q: Why do bigger instruments sound lower?
faq.a: Bigger instruments have longer, heavier strings or longer tubes of air, which vibrate more slowly. Slower vibrations make lower notes.
asks: Why does a double bass sound low?

faq.q: Which string instrument is the lowest?
faq.a: In the orchestra the double bass plays the lowest notes. From high to low the string family is violin, viola, cello and double bass.
asks: What is the biggest string instrument?
Order of string instruments high to low

faq.a: Frequency is how many times something vibrates each second, measured in hertz. Higher frequency means higher pitch. People can hear roughly 20 to 20,000 hertz.

faq.q: How does a guitarist change the pitch?
faq.a: By pressing a string onto the neck, which makes the vibrating part shorter so the note goes higher. Tightening a string also raises its pitch.
asks: Why do you press guitar strings?
How do strings make different notes?

facts: The lowest note on a standard 88-key piano is about 27.5 hertz and the highest is about 4186 hertz.
Young people can typically hear sounds from about 20 to 20,000 hertz.

quiz.say: Look at the 3 instruments. Which one plays the lowest notes?
quiz.why: The double bass has the longest, heaviest strings. They vibrate slowly, so the notes are low.

wrong.1: The violin is the smallest. It plays the highest notes.
wrong.2: The viola is a little bigger than a violin. Its notes are still quite high.

quiz.say: A guitar player makes a string shorter. What happens to the pitch?
quiz.show: 🎸 Shorter string. What happens to the pitch?
quiz.why: A shorter string vibrates faster. Faster vibrations make a higher note.

wrong.1: Lower notes come from longer strings.
wrong.2: A change in length changes the pitch.
